candidates.statement: Effective Date: 2/7/2011; 05/18/2016; 01/21/2022 Page 1 of 5 POLICY AND PROCEDURES OFFICE OF PHARMACEUTICAL QUALITY Applying ICH Q8(R2), Q9(R1), and Q10 Principles to Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls Assessment Table of Contents PURPOSE ...........................................................................1 BACKGROUND ................................................................1 POLICY ..............................................................................2 RESPONSIBILITIES AND PROCEDURES ..................2 REFERENCES...................................................................4 DEFINITIONS ...................................................................4 EFFECTIVE DATE...........................................................5 CHANGE CONTROL TABLE.........................................5 PURPOSE • This MAPP outlines and clarifies how product quality assessors in the Office of Pharmaceutical Quality (OPQ) should apply the recommendations in the ICH Q8(R2), Q9(R1), and Q10 guidances to industry. 1 BACKGROUND • The International Council on Harmonisation (ICH) guidance for industry Q8(R2) Pharmaceutical Development , published on November 20, 2009, provides information on how to present knowledge gained when applying scientific approaches and quality risk management for developing and manufacturing a product. The annex in ICH Q8(R2) further clarifies key concepts outlined in the original guidance published in June 2006 and describes the principles of quality by design (QbD). candidates.context: POLICY • OPQ product quality assessors will consider ICH Q8(R2), Q9(R1), and Q10 recommendations when assessing applications that may or may not include QbD approaches. - Quality target product profile (QTPP). - Critical quality attributes (CQAs) of the drug product.

candidates.statement: - Quality target product profile (QTPP). - Critical quality attributes (CQAs) of the drug product.

candidates.statement: • Critical Quality Attributes (CQA) : A physical, chemical, biological, or microbiological property or characteristic that should be within an appropriate limit, range, or distribution to ensure the desired product quality.
candidates.context: Effective Date: 2/7/2011; 05/18/2016; 01/21/2022 Page 5 of 5 • Quality Target Product Profile (QTPP) : A prospective summary of the quality characteristics of a drug product that ideally will be achieved to ensure the desired quality, taking into account safety and efficacy of the drug product. • Quality by Design (QbD) : A systematic approach to development that begins with predefined objectives and emphasizes product and process understanding and process control based on sound science and quality risk management.

candidates.statement: Design space is proposed by the applicant and is subject to regulatory assessment and approval.
candidates.context: • Design Space : The multidimensional combination and interaction of input variables (e.g., material attributes) and process parameters that have been demonstrated to provide assurance of quality. Working within the design space is not considered as a change. Movement out of the design space is considered to be a change and would normally initiate a regulatory postapproval change process. • Control Strategy : A planned set of controls, derived from current product and process understanding that ensures process performance and product quality.
